messages:
maria_chen: Quick follow-up on the multi-region RFC. I want to nail down the resident-region behavior for customers with data residency requirements. I sketched three operational patterns earlier; want to capture tradeoffs and a preferred default here.

alex_park: TL;DR — I prefer a control-plane pin + proxied writes approach for most cases. It keeps reads fast while ensuring canonical writes go to resident region.

sam_g: Strong caveat: if a tenant forbids ANY cross-region copies then dual-write or async replication are non-starters. We need a tenant-level flag that enforces strict locality.

maria_chen: Right. Proposed states: 
- residency_mode: strict (no cross-region copies; all reads/writes in resident)
- residency_mode: proxy-writes (reads nearest, writes proxied to resident)
- residency_mode: geo-replicated (customer explicitly allows replication)
Which should be the default?

alex_park: Default = proxy-writes. Rationale: best UX for most customers, minimal legal exposure (only one canonical copy), and simpler than full replication.

sam_g: For strict mode we must also forbid cached reads from non-resident regions. That means marking cache entries with resident-region metadata and checking at read time. We'll need a tenant flag `allow_cross_region_reads: true|false`.

maria_chen: Ops question: what happens when resident region is degraded? Two main failover options: 
1) fail-closed (reject write ops) 
2) fail-open to a pre-approved secondary (requires legal signed waiver)
Thoughts?

alex_park: Default fail-closed. Offer fail-open as opt-in with explicit approval workflow and TTL'd waiver artifact. Implementation: control-plane has `failover.mode` per-tenant, can be `closed` or `open`, and if `open` we also store `failover.secondary_region` and `failover.waiver_id`.

sam_g: Telemetry: emit `resident_region`, `write_routed_via_proxy`, and `failover_state` on every write event so auditing and billing can filter by residency.

maria_chen: Good call. Also we need to measure proxy-tail latency. Tyler, any metrics from the staging canary?

tyler_ops: Staging canary (proxy v0.3) results: median write RTT +82ms, P95 +210ms under modest load. No replication divergence observed because we only proxy — no async replication in this mode. Logs and dashboards: https://redwood.internal/infra/canaries/proxy-v0.3

alex_park: Control-plane routing config sketch (YAML):
```
routing_policy:
  read: nearest-region
  write:
    mode: proxy-to-resident
    resident_region: tenant.resident
    failover:
      mode: closed # or open
      secondary_region: null
```
Make sure this is extensible for future `geo-replicated` mode.

maria_chen: Implementation checklist: 
- @alex_park: add RFC appendix describing proxy hop (TLS mutual auth, connection pooling, retry/backoff). Include metrics to track: proxy_call_latency_ms, proxy_error_rate, cross_region_egress_bytes.
- @sam_g: add tenant flag `allow_cross_region_reads` and ensure cache tag checks at read path.
- Ops: tabletop runbook with Legal present for fail-open scenarios.

sam_g: Also add testing matrix: strict-mode unit/integration tests (no exports), proxy-mode latency/load tests, fail-open legal workflow test (simulate waiver issuance and expiry).

maria_chen: Runbook decision: default = proxy-writes + fail-closed; strict mode available; fail-open is opt-in with legal approval. I'll add to RFC follow-up and schedule a 30min sync Monday to finalize.

ops-bot: Runbook stub created: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/multi-region-proxy-failover (internal). Tabletop scheduled: 2026-03-23 15:00 PT.

deploy-bot: Canary rollout proxy-write v0.3 -> staging started at 1792501300. Monitor: /deploys/1792501300.

alex_park: No objections from me. If Legal/Compliance want different defaults for specific geos we can gate via tenant policy.

maria_chen: Thanks all. Agenda for Monday: lock config schema, define SLA text for strict vs proxy modes, and finalize tests + runbook steps. :thumbsup:
